dimension_justifications.soundness: The measurements I could re-derive are exact. I reconstructed all five Store rows of Table 1 from Appendix C, Table 4 by hand (full-prefix 10x2x3.7180 + 30x0.0625 + 30x2.0000 = 136.235; split Q16 = 34.683; frozen = 4.1828 + 2x1.0457 + 6x0.5644 = 9.661; same-memory = 9.395; aggressive = 4.1828 + 2x0.5809 + 3x0.5644 + 3x0.1660 = 7.536), and the all-BF16 re-expression, the 3.5556x/1.8824x format ceilings, and the -0.0585 + -0.3870 = -0.4455 decomposition all close. Every value I spot-checked against claim_evidence_map.tsv agreed to the reported digits (C-QCOMEM-60-STORE-F1-01, C-QCOMEM-60-Q16-SPLIT-01, C-QCOMEM-60-POLICY-TRADEOFF-01, C-H20-DEPLOYMENT-01, C-R34-HYPIC-STORE-01, C-R40-INDEPENDENT-LIVE-BINDING-V29-01, C-R40-PRIMARY-COMPILED-DISPATCH-01, C-R28-SAME-SYSTEM-DETECTOR-01). Against that, three substantive gaps materially reduce confidence in the central claims as stated. (1) Two of the abstract's four headline results -- the operating-point block of Table 1 (full-prefix Q8 at 56.438 MiB, the 5.84x / +3.41 F1 comparison, the j=13 control, all 60-item TTFT) and the Table 18 allocator endpoints (4.901 -> 2.229 GiB final, 4.920 -> 2.843 GiB peak, 54.5%/42.2%) -- have no entry anywhere in the supplied claim index and no row in the paper's own artifact map (Table 30). (2) method_provenance.tsv row M-QCOMEM-DEPLOY-STORE states that the printed Store column is persistent_document_nbytes, not the byte-range union that Sec. 5.1 and the Table 2 caption define it to be; the union is computed under a different field and is not printed. This makes the Appendix H.1 cross-runtime comparison ('under the same byte-range-union estimand', 15.89 vs 139.53 vs 324.09 MiB) rest on a false premise. (3) The ownership discipline of Sec. 4.3 -- the paper's own Read path -- is never executed as specified: the quantized path materializes a full private copy (M-QCOMEM-READ-FORK; disclosed in Sec. 4.3 and 5.6), and the audited path has no split depth and no quantization. The paper is candid about (3); (1) and (2) are not disclosed and are decision-relevant.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Structure, captions and scope tables are unusually disciplined: Table 7 gives a cohort-to-claim authorization matrix with explicit exclusions, Tables 8-9 give per-target coverage/verdict/boundary, and Appendix C prints enough for a reader to check the memory accounting without the artifacts. The cost is a dense, heavily hedged abstract in which four different executions on three different systems are interleaved, so a reader must reconstruct which of the archival run, the operating-point run, the eight-item timing run, or the vLLM factorial each number belongs to. There are localized but real hazards: the vector [8,8,4,4,8,8,8] is introduced in Sec. 4.2 immediately after the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 paragraph and called 'one frozen operating point', while the frozen policy's actual vector [8,8,8,4,8,8,8] appears only inside Figure 2b; the same policy is named 'same-memory mixed' in Table 1 and 'per-layer mixed' in Tables 2 and 21; Table 2's and Table 21's Reduction percentages (88.68-94.01%) are left dtype-mixed with only a verbal caveat while Table 1 carries the corrected column; and 'scientifically valid' rank shards (Sec. 5.5, Appendix A) is never defined.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper explicitly disclaims novelty for its quantizer (Jacob et al. 2018 affine quantizer, FlexGen-style 64-element groups) and for per-layer width assignment (KVTuner, AsymKV), so the contribution is the object quantized -- a heterogeneous hybrid split-replay entry counted under one denominator -- plus an ownership audit harness. That is a genuine but narrow increment. The capacity claim is one selected, non-selection-corrected operating point on one model, one hardware family, two LongBench subsets and 60 items; part of the headline 14.10x is dtype narrowing, which the paper honestly reduces to 10.9965x. Latency is adverse against both endpoints, including against dense recomputation on the operating-point run. The audit component is a validation harness rather than a capability, it is not run on the paper's own quantized path, and its increment over a persistent-base content invariant is, by the authors' own statement, transition-time localization rather than detection. The 54.5%/42.2% allocator saving is shown in the paper's own Table 18 to be exactly matched by a paged-prefix baseline, so it is not an increment either.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem's split-depth residual reuse to a hybrid attention/Gated-DeltaNet backbone (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 10 attention + 30 GDN layers). An offline Write runs a document through layers [0,j), retains the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer full-attention KV and GDN convolution/recurrent state, and group-quantizes all of it with a standard asymmetric affine quantizer over 64-value groups with BF16 scale/bias. An online Read dequantizes the entry, forks it per request, replays the query through the lower layers, and reconstructs the suffix through [j,L). A separate component, ForkAudit, is a phase-indexed ownership/call trace over seven targets (frozen identity, prefix immutability, private ownership, tail-safe COW, host-side launch provenance, cross-arm equivalence, cross-N consistency) with fail-closed coverage semantics. Empirically: on 60 archival Qasper/2WikiMQA items the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy at j=7 retains 9.661 vs 136.235 MiB/document (14.10x; 10.9965x under an all-BF16 reference) at a paired mean F1 delta of -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99]; a separately executed operating-point run adds a quantized exact cache (full-prefix Q8, 56.438 MiB, -3.78 points) making the frozen point 5.84x smaller and 3.41 F1 points higher; timing is adverse (TTFT 0.656 s vs 0.181 s full-prefix and 0.636 s dense); and on a different vLLM+Transformers system with no split depth and no quantization, shared-document KV cuts the post-priming allocator delta by 54.5%/42.2% against a full-copy control, tying the paper's own paged-prefix baseline. The paper claims capacity reduction with an explicit online cost, and explicitly disclaims recall, total VRAM, edge performance, TTFT acceleration and broad quality preservation.
strongest_verified_contribution: The whole-entry memory accounting for a hybrid split-replay entry, and specifically the self-audit in Appendix C. The paper prints per-component byte counts at the cohort mean document length, states the packed-size identity bytes(n,b) = ceil(n/64)(8b+4) with its 3.5556x (b=4) and 1.8824x (b=8) format ceilings, notices that the printed split-to-frozen step of 34.683/9.661 = 3.590x exceeds the Q4 ceiling, and resolves it by showing that 6.000 of the split row's 34.683 MiB is FP32 GDN recurrent state in excess of BF16, giving a within-ceiling 2.969x. I re-derived every row of Table 4 and every Table 1 Store value from the PDF alone, plus the all-BF16 restatement (136.235 -> 106.235, 14.10x -> 10.9965x) and the -0.0585 + -0.3870 = -0.4455 F1 decomposition, and all of it closes. Voluntarily surfacing a dtype confound that cuts your own headline ratio by 22% is rare and is the most credible thing in the paper.
strengths: Claim scoping is exemplary and is itself a reusable artifact. Table 7 authorizes each cohort against a named claim and lists explicit exclusions; Tables 8-9 give per-target coverage, verdict, 'what a pass rules out' and the execution that produced it; claim_evidence_map.tsv carries fourteen explicit 'rejected' rows (C-UNSUPPORTED-*) naming inferences the evidence does not support. I could not find a place where a rejected claim is asserted in the PDF.

The audit/headline system separation is disclosed in every place a reader could look: the abstract ('that factorial runs full-prefix BF16 KV with no split depth and no quantization'), the Figure 1 caption, Sec. 4.4, the Sec. 5.1 'Executed systems' paragraph ('no ForkAudit verdict here covers those packed entries'), Sec. 5.5 and Sec. 5.6. This is the single most common overclaim in audit-plus-system papers and the paper does not make it.

The trusted-computing-base statement in Sec. 4.4 is honest and specific: capture/replay, the mandatory-slot schema, slot-to-live-tensor binding and framework storage semantics are named as trusted, and coherent omission/fabrication, transient writes between observations, compiled GDN, ATen/CUDA and device/driver execution are named as uncovered. Appendix A repeats that 'normal launcher return is not a device-side completion attestation', and the paper calls ForkAudit 'an offline, non-adversarial regression contract, not security attestation'. I found nothing in the PDF that claims more attestation than this admits.

The mutable-code-directory limitation on the archival cohort is disclosed in the main text (Sec. 5.6), in Appendix A with the specific list of unarchived files, in Appendix I, and in Table 7's 'not source-frozen regeneration'. Appendix A goes further than most papers would and states the consequence outright: those files 'must be released before Table 1 is independently re-executable'.

Negative and adverse results are reported rather than buried: TTFT is worse than dense recomputation as well as worse than exact caching; the aggressive policy's interval excludes zero; the audit's alias finding is explicitly reduced to localization rather than exclusive detection because a persistent-base content invariant catches it too; the 54.5%/42.2% allocator gain is stated to tie the paper's own paged-prefix baseline and to lose on generation increment (1.950 vs 0.019 GiB).

Appendix B reports all 42 paired-bootstrap intervals including the 24 archival ones that used a different reference arm, explicitly so that none is 'computed but unreported', and states that the reference-arm change made the previously published loss 13% larger.
questions: What is the run identifier of the operating-point execution referenced in the Reproducibility Statement, and what is its package alias and manifest SHA-256? It is not printed in the PDF, has no row in Table 30, and has no entry in claim_evidence_map.tsv, yet it supplies the abstract's 5.84x / +3.41 F1 comparison, the j=13 control and every 60-item TTFT value.

Sec. 5.1 and the Table 2 caption define Store as 'the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry'. method_provenance.tsv M-QCOMEM-DEPLOY-STORE states the printed column is persistent_document_nbytes and that the byte-range union is a separate field, persistent_total_resident_nbytes, that is not printed. Which is it, and if the printed column is the nbytes sum, does the Appendix H.1 comparison against SGLang/HYPIC page-granular receipts still hold 'under the same byte-range-union estimand'?

What generation budget did the archival 60-item block of Table 1 use? Sec. 5.1 says it ran 'on the stack of Table 2', whose caption says 'at most 32 generated tokens', but it distinguishes the operating-point run by 'dataset-length generation'; M-QCOMEM-READ-GREEDY records max_new_tokens 128 for Qasper and 32 for 2WikiMQA. If the archival block used 128 for Qasper, the caption cross-reference is wrong.

Was the reported F1 computed by LongBench/metrics.py::qa_f1_score, as reference Bai et al. 2024b and Appendix A ('its official F1 implementation') state, or by the authors' own answer_f1 in run_downstream.py/verify.py, as M-QCOMEM-F1 states, with ASCII-only punctuation stripping and empty cases returning float(pred_tokens == ref_tokens)? These differ on empty predictions, which matters on short-answer 2WikiMQA items.

The bootstrap is specified in the PDF as '10,000 paired item-level resamples, seed 20260902' with percentile endpoints. M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP records a Python random.Random drawing indices one at a time and index selection int(0.025*(n-1))/int(0.975*(n-1)), and says the interval 'is reproducible only for this exact seed sequence and repetition count'. Which script produced the 18 new intervals, and is it archived? M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP marks analyze_validation.py and aggregate_replay.py as NOT ARCHIVED.

Is the accompanying research package part of this submission? The paper cites package paths, registry entries and manifest hashes throughout Appendix J and tells reviewers to 'verify each package by content hash', but never states that the package is attached, submitted, or will be released.

Sec. 4.2 introduces widths [8,8,4,4,8,8,8] as 'one frozen operating point' directly after the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 paragraph, but Figure 2b shows the frozen policy as [8,8,8,4,8,8,8] and Appendix C attributes [8,8,4,4,8,8,8] to the same-memory row. Can Sec. 4.2 name the row each vector belongs to, and can Table 1's 'same-memory mixed' and Table 2's 'per-layer mixed' be given one name?
What does 'scientifically valid' mean as a shard property (Sec. 5.5, Appendix A)? It is used as a verdict term but is never defined in the PDF.

The eleven method_provenance.tsv rows marked 'NOT ARCHIVED in this repository' cite an absolute path under a named personal home directory. Is method_provenance.tsv intended to ship with the anonymous supplement, and if so has it been scrubbed?

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p. 6); Table 2 caption footnote (p. 7); Sec. 5.6 para. 2 (p. 9); Appendix H.1 text (p. 29); Table 21 footnote
issues.observed_evidence: The PDF defines the estimand three times as a byte-range union: Sec. 5.1 'In both deployment tables "Store" is the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry'; Table 2 footnote 'Store is the byte-range union owned by one retained entry'; Sec. 5.6 'Store, the entry-owned physical byte-range union'. method_provenance.tsv M-QCOMEM-DEPLOY-STORE states the opposite for Table 2: 'The eight-item deployment table's Store column is persistent_document_nbytes, which is the same residual.nbytes + PackedCache.nbytes formula as the 60-item panel ... the byte-range union it also computes is persistent_total_resident_nbytes and is not the printed column', and concludes 'Table 2's caption claim that Store is the physical byte-range union is therefore not what the printed column measures.' For the 60-item panel, M-QCOMEM-STORE-ACCOUNTANT describes a hybrid: the residual term is numel*element_size while the cache term is untyped_storage().nbytes() deduplicated by (device, data_ptr, storage_nbytes).
issues.why_it_matters: Appendix H.1 uses the byte-range-union framing to license the only cross-system retained-state comparison in the paper: '139.53 MiB and 324.09 MiB, against 15.89 MiB for Q-CoMem Q8 under the same byte-range estimand', and the 0.58% agreement between 139.53 and 140.34 MiB is offered as bounding the cross-runtime inclusion-rule discrepancy. If the in-process column is an nbytes sum rather than a union, that premise is wrong and the SGLang/HYPIC comparison is between two different estimands. Under a union, padding, non-exact storage allocation and shared backing all count differently, which is exactly what the paper argues distinguishes page-quantized SGLang receipts from element-exact in-process payload.
issues.required_fix: State the estimand exactly as implemented in Sec. 5.1, the Table 2 caption and Sec. 5.6 -- for the deployment table, deduplicated packed-leaf nbytes; for the 60-item panel, the residual-nbytes-plus-deduplicated-storage-nbytes hybrid -- and either print persistent_total_resident_nbytes alongside it or drop the byte-range-union language from the Appendix H.1 cross-runtime comparison.
issues.verification_test: For the eight deployment documents, emit both persistent_document_nbytes and persistent_total_resident_nbytes per configuration and show the two columns; if they differ anywhere, the union claim is falsified for that row. Independently, recompute Store for one item from the archived shard fields using the printed definition and require exact agreement.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-item dual-column Store export for the eight-item cohort, and the storage-inventory records behind persistent_total_resident_nbytes.

issues.location: Reproducibility Statement (p. 10); Appendix A paras. 1-2 (p. 14); Appendix J 'Artifact aliases' and Table 30 (pp. 34-36)
issues.observed_evidence: The paper promises a package and never says what a reader gets. Appendix J refers throughout to 'the accompanying research package', gives relative paths rooted in it, and instructs that 'A reviewer verifies each package by content hash rather than by path'. But grep over the full PDF text for 'supplement', 'available', 'upon acceptance', 'will be released' and 'anonymous repository' returns nothing outside the 'Anonymous authors' byline. Meanwhile Appendix A concedes that the package 'archives the quantizer/split-replay module and the prompt-and-scoring driver byte-identically at four paths, but not the run driver, the aggregation and bootstrap scripts, the layer-policy search, the deployment accountant, or the launch script; an artifact reviewer can therefore read the code those files call but not the files that produced the table, and they must be released before Table 1 is independently re-executable.' issues.why_it_matters: The reproducibility posture as written is a set of internal paths and hashes with no stated distribution. issues.required_fix: Add an explicit availability statement to the Reproducibility Statement saying whether the package accompanies this submission, what it contains, and what it omits; move Appendix A's 'must be released before Table 1 is independently re-executable' sentence into the Reproducibility Statement verbatim; and either archive the six named missing files or state plainly that Table 1 is replayable-from-outcomes but not re-executable.
issues.verification_test: Hand a third party only the PDF and the stated package, and ask them to (a) locate the artifact and (b) regenerate any single Table 1 cell from source. Step (b) must fail under the current package by the paper's own Appendix A admission; the fix is verified when the Reproducibility Statement predicts that failure.

issues.location: Sec. 4.2 (Eq. 3, p. 4); Sec. 4.2 last para. and Figure 2b (p. 5); Sec. 5.1; Sec. 5.4; Table 1 footnote
issues.observed_evidence: Of the six named method components, only some are code-backed. Archived and traceable: the quantizer (M-QCOMEM-EQ3-QUANTIZER, quantize_residual L98-139 / quantize_tensor L186-252), the dequantizer, the pack codec, the Write path (write_lower_replay L796-820), the Read fork/replay/suffix/greedy path, and the F1 scorer (run_downstream.py answer_f1, verify.py). Not archived: eleven rows carry the literal marker 'NOT ARCHIVED in this repository (live implementation tree ...)', covering the split depth j=7 (M-QCOMEM-SPLIT-DEPTH: 'neither run_replay_diagnostic.py nor launch_mixed_validation_8gpu.sh is archived here'), all three bit policies, the policy search, the group-size-64 verification, the Store accountant runner, the deployment accountant, the greedy/timing driver, and the bootstrap (M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP: 'analyze_validation.py and aggregate_replay.py'). The two undisclosed quantizer behaviours also matter: s = 1 on degenerate groups changes reconstruction for constant groups, and edge-value padding changes the element count n that Appendix C's ceil(n/64)(8b+4) identity is evaluated on.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Quality cohort' and 'Latency execution' (p. 6); Table 2 caption (p. 7); Sec. 5.4; Appendix B para. 3; Table 5 (p. 18)
issues.observed_evidence: The re-run recipe is complete for the audit stack and incomplete for the stack that produces the headline numbers. Table 5 gives the ForkAudit factorial Python 3.11.13, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.14.1, vLLM 0.26.0+cu129, Triton 3.6.0, CUDA 12.9. Table 2, the stack behind Tables 1 and 2, gives only 'Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu129, Transformers 5.14.1, one H20-3e per item' -- no Python version, no CUDA version, no model revision (M-QCOMEM-PANEL-RUNNER records revision 59d61f3, which never appears in the PDF). The generation budget for Table 1's archival block is never stated: Sec. 5.1 says it ran 'on the stack of Table 2', whose caption says 'at most 32 generated tokens', but distinguishes the operating-point run by 'dataset-length generation', while M-QCOMEM-READ-GREEDY records 'max_new_tokens 128 for Qasper and 32 for 2WikiMQA'. The aggregation rule is given for Table 1 (60-item means) and Table 2 (medians over eight documents), which is good, but the bootstrap procedure is under-specified: the PDF gives repetitions, seed and 'percentile interval', whereas M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP records a Python random.Random drawing indices one at a time with index selection int(0.025*(n-1)) / int(0.975*(n-1)) and states the endpoints are 'reproducible only for this exact seed sequence and repetition count'.
issues.why_it_matters: Seed plus resample count does not determine percentile endpoints across RNG implementations; a re-implementer using numpy would get different endpoints at the same nominal seed and would wrongly conclude the interval failed to replicate. The missing generation budget is worse: if Qasper items generated 128 tokens rather than 32, both the F1 means and the TTFT/throughput comparison in Sec. 5.3 are being read against a caption that says otherwise. The missing model revision means a re-executor cannot even pin the checkpoint.
issues.required_fix: Add the model revision, Python and CUDA versions and the per-dataset generation budget to the Table 2 caption or Sec. 5.1; correct or qualify the 'on the stack of Table 2' cross-reference if the archival block's generation budget differs; and specify the bootstrap RNG (library, generator, draw order) and the exact order-statistic indices in Appendix B.
issues.verification_test: Re-run the frozen row on a clean machine from the PDF's stated settings alone and require mean F1 54.24 +/- rounding and TTFT within the reported spread; independently, reimplement the bootstrap from Appendix B's text with numpy and check whether it lands on [-2.06, 0.99] -- if it does not, the specification is incomplete.
issues.evidence_needed: A single environment/settings block covering model revision, framework and CUDA versions, per-dataset generation budget, truncation rule, and the exact bootstrap RNG contract.

issues.location: Sec. 4.3 (p. 5); Sec. 4.4 (p. 5); Sec. 5.1 'Executed systems' (p. 6); Sec. 5.6 para. 3 (p. 9); Figure 1 caption; Table 7 rows 'Primary ownership factorial' and 'H20 archival Store-F1 validation'
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's named Read path is defined in Sec. 4.3 as a logical fork F_r(D) in which document state K_l^D, G_l^D 'is immutable and may be shared', a borrowed recurrent base 'must rebind to private storage', and 'a partial KV tail is copied before append'. M-QCOMEM-READ-FORK states that in the executed path 'This is a full materialize-per-query fork. In this Table 1/Table 2 PyTorch path there is no shared immutable document state, no borrowed recurrent base and no copy-on-write tail ... The borrow/rebind/tail-COW discipline described in Sec. 4.3 belongs to the separate vLLM paged implementation (qcomem_vllm_paged_kernel.py), not to this path.' The audit-side rows (M-KV-FORK, M-TAIL-COW, M-GDN) point at that separate implementation, which per Sec. 5.1 and Table 7 runs full-prefix BF16 KV with no split depth and no quantization. So the discipline is specified in one system, audited in a second, and the quantized capacity result is measured in a third configuration that implements neither. The paper states this in Sec. 4.3, 4.4, 5.1 and 5.6, and Sec. 5.6 concedes 'ownership there transfers by design argument only'.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's integrated contribution -- quantized hybrid split-replay entries that are safely shareable across concurrent requests -- is never executed end to end. Each half exists; the composition does not. This bounds the significance of the whole design, since the capacity numbers come from a full-copy-per-query implementation whose per-request cost the paper does not report, and the audit's ownership guarantees attach to a configuration with no packed entry at all. Sec. 4.4 already lists the untested packed-entry obligations (dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding, packed-entry lifetime).
issues.required_fix: Either run the ownership factorial on a packed j=7 Q4/Q4/Q8 entry so at least one cell exercises dequantize-then-share, or, if that is out of scope, state in the abstract and Sec. 1 contribution bullets that the two halves are never composed in any executed configuration -- the current bullets say the audit is 'off the quantized path' but not that no executed system implements Sec. 4.3's fork on a packed entry.
issues.verification_test: Add one factorial cell with split depth 7 and Q4/Q4/Q8 packing and run targets 2-4 (prefix immutability, private ownership, tail-safe COW) on it; a pass on that cell would be the first evidence that the composed design holds.
issues.evidence_needed: One ForkAudit cell on a packed entry, plus per-request allocator cost of the current materialize-per-query fork at N > 1.

issues.location: Sec. 4.2 last para. (p. 5); Figure 2b; Table 1 row 'same-memory mixed'; Table 2 row 'per-layer mixed'; Table 21; Appendix C para. 3
issues.observed_evidence: Sec. 4.2 states 'The reported per-layer policy uses a Q4 residual and active-layer widths [8,8,4,4,8,8,8] ... we treat it as one frozen operating point', placed one paragraph after 'The evaluated Q4/Q4/Q8 point'. Per M-QCOMEM-POLICY-FROZEN the headline frozen policy is [8,8,8,4,8,8,8]; [8,8,4,4,8,8,8] is the same-memory policy (M-QCOMEM-POLICY-SAMEMEM). The frozen vector appears in the PDF only inside Figure 2b's bit strip. The same policy is called 'same-memory mixed' in Table 1 (9.395 MiB) and 'per-layer mixed' in Tables 2 and 21 (9.74 MiB), and the aggressive vector [8,8,2,2,2,8,2] is only described verbally in Appendix C. I confirmed the mapping by reconstruction: Appendix C's stated composition for the same-memory row ('moves layer 2 to Q4') gives 4.1828 + 2x1.0457 + 5x0.5644 + 0.2988 = 9.395, and for the aggressive row gives 7.536.
issues.why_it_matters: The word 'frozen' is load-bearing in this paper -- it is the headline policy's name -- and Sec. 4.2 applies it to a different vector than Figure 2b assigns it. A reader taking Sec. 4.2 at face value will attribute the 14.10x / -0.45 result to [8,8,4,4,8,8,8], which is the row with the worse F1 delta and one catastrophic item.
issues.required_fix: In Sec. 4.2, print all three vectors in a small table with the row name each belongs to; adopt one name per policy across Tables 1, 2 and 21.
issues.verification_test: Check that every occurrence of a bit vector in the PDF is adjacent to the Table 1 row name it denotes, and that Table 1 and Table 2 use identical policy names.

issues.location: Table 2 'Reduction' column (p. 7); Table 21 footnote (p. 28); Appendix H.1 (p. 29); Sec. 5.5 and Appendix A ('scientifically valid')
issues.observed_evidence: Table 1 carries a full all-BF16 correction in its footnote (106.235/28.683/9.661/9.395/7.536 and 1.00/3.7038/10.9965/11.3073/14.0969x). Table 2 does not: its Reduction column prints 88.68%/92.87%/93.06%/94.01% against the 140.34 MiB native-dtype reference with only the verbal note that '42.8% of its 140.34 MiB is FP32 GDN recurrent state'. Table 21 repeats '88.68%/93.06%' uncorrected, and Appendix H.1's cross-runtime levels (15.89 vs 139.53 vs 324.09 MiB) are likewise stated against native-dtype references. Separately, Sec. 5.5 and Appendix A describe rank shards as 'scientifically valid' without defining the term anywhere in the PDF.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper went to real trouble to correct the dtype confound in Table 1 and then leaves the same confound uncorrected in the three tables a reader is most likely to quote for cross-system comparison. Roughly 30 of the 140.34 MiB reference is FP32 excess, so the 88.68-94.01% figures overstate the packing contribution by the same mechanism Appendix C dissects. An undefined verdict term in a paper whose whole thesis is precise evidence semantics is a small but jarring lapse.
issues.required_fix: Add an all-BF16 corrected column or footnote figure to Table 2 and Table 21 matching Table 1's treatment, note the same correction where Appendix H.1 states the three levels, and define 'scientifically valid' at first use or replace it with the concrete condition it stands for.
issues.verification_test: Confirm that every reduction ratio in the paper is printed under a stated dtype convention, and that no undefined verdict term appears in Sec. 5.5 or Appendix A.
issues.evidence_needed: None; the corrected values are already derivable from Table 4.

issues.location: method_provenance.tsv, 11 rows (M-QCOMEM-GROUP-64, M-QCOMEM-READ-GREEDY, M-QCOMEM-SPLIT-DEPTH, M-QCOMEM-POLICY-FROZEN, M-QCOMEM-POLICY-SAMEMEM, M-QCOMEM-POLICY-AGGRESSIVE, M-QCOMEM-POLICY-CALIBRATION, M-QCOMEM-STORE-ACCOUNTANT, M-QCOMEM-DEPLOY-STORE, M-QCOMEM-BOOTSTRAP, M-QCOMEM-PANEL-RUNNER); Appendix J 'Artifact aliases' (p. 34)
issues.observed_evidence: Eleven method_provenance.tsv rows cite an absolute path under a personal home directory that names a real user, e.g. 'NOT ARCHIVED in this repository (live implementation tree /Users/<name>/MacLLM-Bench/gpu)'. M-QCOMEM-POLICY-CALIBRATION additionally cites an internal job/trial identifier ('QuickSilver job 233909 / trial 1827870, completed 2026-08-11T15:52:45Z'). This sits directly against Appendix J's stated policy that 'Aliases replace the internal directory names used during development; they carry no ordering, date, or platform information, and no path here resolves to an external service.'
issues.why_it_matters: Under double-blind review, a supplement artifact carrying a home-directory username is a de-anonymization vector, and it contradicts the paper's own stated aliasing discipline. Appendix J names claim_evidence_map.tsv as a shipped artifact; whether method_provenance.tsv ships is not stated, but it was supplied to reviewers here.
issues.required_fix: Scrub absolute host paths and internal job identifiers from every provenance artifact intended for the supplement, replacing them with the neutral aliases Appendix J already defines, and state in Appendix J which provenance files ship.
issues.verification_test: grep the shipped supplement for '/Users/', '/home/', and internal scheduler job identifiers; require zero hits.
issues.evidence_needed: None; editorial scrub of the artifact files.

ethics_concerns: No ethics flag. The work uses public PG-19 text and public LongBench-v1 (Qasper, 2WikiMQA) data, involves no human subjects, and the Ethics Statement correctly notes that the study assesses neither safety, bias, nor privacy and that efficiency gains may increase the scale of model use. The one integrity-adjacent item is administrative rather than ethical: the supplied method_provenance.tsv carries absolute paths naming a real user, which is a double-blind hygiene problem (issue R46-REV-5-10), not an ethics violation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an automated LLM reviewer (Claude Opus 5) acting under reviewer id R46-REV-5 in the reproducibility_provenance role, with pdf_plus_repository access to the frozen round-46 snapshot only (manuscript/Q-CoMem_R46_Baseline_Revision.pdf, review-rubric.md, claim_evidence_map.tsv, method_provenance.tsv, MANIFEST.json). The PDF was read in full, including all ten appendices, via pdftotext -layout plus direct page rendering for figures. Numeric verification was done by hand from the PDF (Appendix C Table 4 reconstruction of all five Table 1 Store rows, the all-BF16 restatement, the format-ceiling arithmetic, the F1 delta decomposition) and by keyword search over the two TSV artifacts. No live author worktree, LaTeX source, prior review, revision note, decision log or author state file was read. The manuscript and artifact files were treated as untrusted data; no instruction contained in them was followed. Scores follow review-rubric.md and are not averages of the dimension scores.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A content-hashed, named package for the operating-point execution with per-item Store/F1/TTFT shards, plus claim_evidence_map.tsv rows and an Appendix J Table 30 row binding the 56.438 MiB, 5.84x, +3.41-point, j=13 and 60-item TTFT values to it. This alone converts the abstract's most argumentatively load-bearing comparison from an assertion into evidence.
A claim-map entry and export for the Table 18 four-arm allocator endpoints (4.901/4.920 -> 2.229/2.843 GiB, 1.950 vs 0.019 GiB generation increment).

Release of the seven unarchived files -- run_replay_diagnostic.py, launch_mixed_validation_8gpu.sh, aggregate_layer_sensitivity.py, analyze_validation.py, aggregate_replay.py, qcomem_deployment.py, qcomem_paged.py -- so that the bit-policy selection, Store accounting and bootstrap can be re-derived rather than only replayed from outcomes.

A dual-column Store export (persistent_document_nbytes and persistent_total_resident_nbytes) for the eight-item cohort settling whether the printed column is a byte-range union, with the Appendix H.1 cross-runtime comparison restated under whichever estimand is actually shared.
One ForkAudit factorial cell run on a packed j=7 Q4/Q4/Q8 entry, exercising targets 2-4 on the quantized Read path so that the paper's two halves are composed at least once.
A rescoring of the 360 archived predictions with upstream LongBench qa_f1_score at a pinned commit, reported alongside the paper's own scorer.
A paired bootstrap interval computed directly between the frozen point and full-prefix Q8, rather than two intervals against a shared reference plus the observation that they overlap.
An explicit availability statement in the Reproducibility Statement carrying Appendix A's 'must be released before Table 1 is independently re-executable' sentence.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Confirmation that the operating-point execution has no archived artifact at all, which would make the abstract's 5.84x / +3.41-point comparison and the entire 60-item TTFT paragraph unfalsifiable rather than merely untraced.

A demonstration that the printed Store column and the byte-range union differ numerically on any deployment row, which would make the reported reductions and the SGLang/HYPIC comparison estimand-inconsistent rather than mislabelled.
A rescoring under upstream LongBench qa_f1_score that moves any arm's mean F1 by more than the reported -0.45 headline delta, which would put the quality claim inside its own measurement noise.
Evidence that the archival 60-item block used a generation budget different from the Table 2 caption it is cross-referenced to, without that being stated.
Any instance of a C-UNSUPPORTED-* rejected claim being asserted in the manuscript, or of a manuscript number disagreeing with the value in its own claim-map row.
Evidence that the materialize-per-query Read fork used in Tables 1 and 2 makes resident-set cost scale with N in a way that erases the per-document capacity advantage under any realistic concurrency.
review_limitations: Access was PDF plus two provenance TSVs and a manifest. I could not open any source file, evidence package, shard or manifest referenced by claim_evidence_map.tsv or method_provenance.tsv, so every judgement about what the code does rests on the provenance rows' own descriptions, which are themselves author-supplied and untrusted.

Where the PDF and method_provenance.tsv disagree (the Store estimand, the F1 scorer attribution, the archival generation budget), I could not adjudicate which is correct; I report the disagreement and its consequences rather than asserting the artifact is right.

Absence of a claim_evidence_map.tsv entry proves the supplied index does not cover a number; it does not prove no artifact exists elsewhere. I have scored the traceability gap, not asserted the run did not happen.

I verified the memory accounting arithmetic exhaustively but did not attempt to validate the F1 values, bootstrap endpoints, timing measurements or allocator snapshots, none of which is checkable from the PDF.

My assessment of novelty relative to KVTuner, AsymKV, KIVI, Quamba2, Marconi and HYPIC rests on the paper's own related-work characterizations plus Table 19; I did not read those papers in this review.
